deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the existence proof for the definite integral of a continuous function, given as a preliminary in Riemann's treatment of trigonometric series. The previous page sets up the Riemann sums. Take a = x_0 < x_1 < ... < x_{n-1} < x_n = b and points x_{k-1} < xi_k < x_k. The sum is S = sum_k (x_k - x_{k-1}) f(xi_k). For a fixed delta, let M = M(delta) be the largest and m = m(delta) the smallest value S can take over all partitions whose intervals are all shorter than delta and over all choices of the xi_k. Then m <= S <= M.

(1) Monotonicity. Suppose delta is decreased. Every admissible partition for the smaller delta was already admissible for the larger one. So the set of attainable values of S shrinks. Hence the largest value M cannot increase and the smallest value m cannot decrease. This excludes the alternative raised at the top of the page, in which the values of S would not settle down.

(2) M - m -> 0. Let M be realised by the partition x'_k with points xi'_k:
M = (x'_1 - a) f(xi'_1) + (x'_2 - x'_1) f(xi'_2) + ... + (b - x'_{n-1}) f(xi'_n).
Let m be realised by the partition x''_k with points xi''_k:
m = (x''_1 - a) f(xi''_1) + ...

(3) Common refinement. Merge all x' and x'' and order them by size; call them v_1 < v_2 < ... < v_p. Each difference x'_k - x'_{k-1} is then replaced by a sum of consecutive differences v_j - v_{j-1}, namely the x'' falling between x'_{k-1} and x'_k. The tag f(xi'_k) is repeated on each piece, so several consecutive xi' coincide. This gives
M = (v_1 - a) f(xi'_1) + (v_2 - v_1) f(xi'_2) + ... ,
and in the same way
m = (v_1 - a) f(xi''_1) + (v_2 - v_1) f(xi''_2) + ... ,
with the tags re-indexed by refined interval.

(4) Subtracting term by term:
M - m = (v_1 - a)(f(xi'_1) - f(xi''_1)) + (v_2 - v_1)(f(xi'_2) - f(xi''_2)) + ... + (b - v_p)(f(xi'_{p+1}) - f(xi''_{p+1})).

(5) Estimate. In the first partition, xi'_k lies in the same interval as v_{k-1} and v_k. That interval is shorter than delta, so xi'_k differs from each of them by at most delta. The same holds for xi''_k in the second partition. Hence |xi'_k - xi''_k| <= 2 delta. Let d be the largest change of f when x changes by at most 2 delta. Then every difference f(xi'_k) - f(xi''_k) < d.

(6) Implied conclusion (mine; it lies off the page). M - m < d (b - a), and d -> 0 as delta -> 0 by continuity. Since M decreases, m increases and M - m -> 0, both converge to a common limit, the integral (the area).

The next page applies this to the Dirichlet-kernel proof of convergence of Fourier series.
errors: The argument assumes the largest and smallest values M, m are actually attained by some partition and tag choice. In general they are only a supremum and infimum (mesh < delta is an open condition). The proof is easily repaired with near-extremal sums or with an epsilon.

The final step needs d(2 delta) -> 0, i.e. uniform continuity on [a,b]. The continuity definition on the previous page is pointwise in form, and uniform continuity is used tacitly without proof, as in Cauchy (1823). It was first proved by Heine (1872).
There is an edge bookkeeping slip: the last term is written (b - v_p) with tags indexed p, but there are p+1 refined intervals. This is notational only.
Minor: the indexing xi'_k versus the refined index (repeated tags) is only described verbally. This is acceptable.

results.what: Existence of the definite integral of a continuous function as the limit of sums sum (x_k - x_{k-1}) f(xi_k) as the mesh tends to 0, via the sup/inf of the sums over partitions of mesh < delta, monotonicity in delta, common refinement, and the bound M - m <= (b-a) * oscillation over 2 delta.
results.modern_name: Existence of the Riemann integral for continuous functions (Cauchy-sum / Darboux upper-lower bound via common refinement and uniform continuity)
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy (Résumé des leçons, 1823) for continuous functions; Riemann (Habilitationsschrift 1854) for the general integral concept; Darboux (1875) for upper/lower sums; Heine (1872) for uniform continuity

results.what: Monotonicity of the extremal values of Riemann sums as the mesh bound delta decreases (admissible sets are nested).
results.modern_name: Monotone convergence of upper/lower envelopes of Riemann sums (limsup/liminf over the mesh)
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Cauchy; made explicit by Darboux 1875

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard lecture-style proof of the existence of the integral for continuous functions, essentially Cauchy's 1823 argument. It is used as preliminary material for Riemann's Fourier-series lectures, whose content is known from his published work and the Hattendorff lecture edition. The sup/inf-over-mesh framing has a mild Darboux flavour, but it is not beyond what Riemann is known to have done.

checkable.asserts: For f=x**2 on [0,1] with a uniform partition, the upper minus lower sum equals 1/n, which tends to 0 (an instance of M - m -> 0).
The 2*delta oscillation of x**2 near x is 4*d*x+4*d**2, which is bounded on [0,1] by 4d+4d^2 -> 0. This is the modulus d(2 delta) used in the bound M - m <= (b-a) d.
Refining an interval and repeating its tag value leaves the Riemann sum unchanged (common-refinement step).

transcription_corrections: 'wird also höchstens um 1/2 M' should most likely read 'wird also höchstens = M' (the largest value is at most M), i.e. 'can therefore not increase'.
'daß S den kleinsten Werth M an nicht' should be 'den größten Werth M annimmt' (M is the largest value); the sentence is mostly struck through.
The opening line likely discusses whether the individual values of S approach one another, versus the alternative that they do not ('...sich um endlich mehr nähern').
'Es nun zu beweisen' should be 'Um nun zu beweisen'.
'die größte Änderung der f(x) welche dann wird x um 2δ' should read roughly 'welche stattfindet, wenn x um 2δ geändert wird'.
